import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 839

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/839](https://www.erdosproblems.com/839)
- [Er78f] Erdős, P., *Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on
  Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).

See also [Erdős Problem 359](https://www.erdosproblems.com/359) and
[Erdős Problem 867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867).
-/

open Filter Real Finset
open scoped ENNReal

namespace Erdos839

/-- A sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is "sum-of-consecutive-free" if no term equals
the sum of a contiguous block of earlier terms. That is, for all $i$,
$a_i \neq a_j + a_{j+1} + \cdots + a_k$ for any $j \leq k < i$. -/
def SumOfConsecutiveFree (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, ∀ j k : ℕ, j ≤ k → k < i →
    a i ≠ ∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc j k, a l

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 1) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\limsup a_n / n = \infty$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ≥0∞) / n) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 2, stronger) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log x} \sum_{a_n < x} \frac{1}{a_n} = 0$?

This is equivalent to asking whether the range $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}$ has logarithmic density zero
(see `Set.HasLogDensity`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    Set.HasLogDensity (Set.range a) 0 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Formalize the additional material on the possible lower limit, reciprocal-sum growth,
-- upper-density constructions, and the links with Erdős Problems 359 and 867.

end Erdos839

findings.description: The bibliography at lines 24–25 identifies [Er78f] as “Problems in number theory and combinatorics,” in the Sixth Manitoba conference proceedings. The [Er78f] reference used by the cited problem page is a different paper: “On some unusual nonconventional problems in additive number theory,” Mat. Lapok 30 (1978/82), 9–14. Its equation (4), on page 9, states the two questions formalized here. The mathematical statements are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Er78f supplies the correct title and publication. The original article, titled “Néhány szokatlan, nem konvencionális, additív számelméleti problémáról,” appears on pp. 9–14 of https://real-j.mtak.hu/9378/1/MTA_MatematikaiLapok_1978-1982.pdf; equation (4) gives the infinite limsup and the normalized reciprocal-sum limit.

Its original scan at https://hrj.episciences.org/125/pdf confirms the title and publication; section 4, pp. 42–43, asks whether consecutive-sum-free sequences have lower density zero and, more strongly, logarithmic density zero.

reformulations.difference: The source indexes its sequence from 1 and writes an infinite limsup. Lean indexes from 0 and uses ENNReal division, making the quotient at index 0 infinite under the positivity hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The value at index 0 does not affect the tail limsup. For n≥1, a(n)/(n+1) ≤ a(n)/n ≤ 2a(n)/(n+1), so the ratios with denominators n and n+1 are unbounded on every tail simultaneously. Relabeling a(n) as the source's a_{n+1} preserves the hypotheses. In scratch.lean, zero_based_limsup_equivalence proves that the exact Lean limsup conclusion is equivalent to ∀ R≥0, ∀ N, ∃ n≥N, R<a(n)/(n+1), with real-valued quotients.

reformulations.difference: Set.HasLogDensity uses integer cutoffs k≤n and sums over the range set, whereas the source uses real x→∞ and sums over sequence terms satisfying a_n<x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Strict monotonicity gives injectivity, so summing over the range counts each sequence term exactly once. At integer n≥2, changing <n to ≤n changes the normalized sum by either zero or 1/(n log n), which tends to zero. For real x≥2, put m=floor(x): the nonnegative strict-cutoff sum divided by log x is at most the inclusive-cutoff sum at m divided by log m. This proves the real limit from the integer limit; restricting the real limit to integers and applying the endpoint estimate proves the converse. logarithmic_source_equivalence in logdensity.lean proves the full equivalence to the source's real-x, strict-cutoff sequence sum.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the definition or either theorem. All quantifiers, hypotheses, answer scopes, interval bounds, and limiting conventions were checked. Lean experiments verified that powers of two satisfy all hypotheses, singleton-block exclusions are redundant under strict monotonicity, and the initial zero-denominator cases do not change the limits. Both scratch files compile without errors or warnings; the equivalence proofs depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, not sorryAx. The source still marks both questions open; Freud's counterexample concerns the additional, unformalized upper-density conjecture. Erdős Problems pages were read through r.jina.ai after direct requests encountered Cloudflare challenges. No repository files were edited.
